enalapriril is an effective antihypertensive agent in the Dahl rat model of genetic hypertension.

the development of a new class of drugs, angiotensin II converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of enalapril on SBP are not related to its action as a CE inhibitor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enalaprial may lower SBP via a mechanism independent of angiotensin II.
enalapriI lowers SBP by mechanisms related to an action at a CEI site and by mechanisms unrelated to an action at CEI sites.
the effects of enalapril in the DS and DR rats on 0, 0.4 and 8.0 % NaCl are not related to its ability to inhibit angiotensin-converting enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be careful about how we define the “normal” range of blood pressure in different age groups, because the normal range is likely to be different for different populations.
the use of enalapril in patients with hypertension and diabetes is not contraindicated, but it should be monitored for the development of hyperkalemia.
we need to do more research on the effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors in the treatment of hypertension in patients with diabetes mellitus.
